Commentary.Commentary: Right then, a comfortable win for Sri Lanka puts them in a very strong position as they still have a couple of games to play. They have a quick turnaround as they play against Hong Kong, China, in Dubai on 15th September, Monday. But for Bangladesh, the way forward has got a bit more challenging, with just one match remaining. They find themselves in the do-or-die territory now. They play against Afghanistan on Tuesday, 16th September. So far, this Asia Cup hasn't produced any nervy games, with all being one-sided. But that, surely and hopefully, won't be the case on Sunday, 14th September, as we wait for the clash of the ages. Next up, it is time for India vs Pakistan at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. The first ball of this marquee Group A match is scheduled to be bowled at 8 pm IST (2.30 pm GMT). But do make sure to mark your presence an hour earlier for the exciting build-up and analysis. Till then, we sign off from here. Take care, cheers!

The victorious skipper of Sri Lanka, CHARITH ASALANKA, says that the first two overs were the key moment with two wickets and two maidens there, setting up the platform perfectly and giving them a dream start. Speaking about Wanindu Hasaranga, he mentions that his googly remains his biggest weapon, one that even teammates struggle to pick at times. Calls Hasaranga a real superstar. On batting and improving the net run rate, Asalanka adds that once they got to around 115-120, the focus was on finishing the game quickly. Also, thanks to the fans, he says that the atmosphere was absolutely brilliant with tremendous support from both Sri Lankan and Bangladeshi supporters.

The captain of Bangladesh, LITTON DAS, reflects on the defeat. He admits they lost the game inside the Powerplay itself with the bat. Adds that had they scored anything around 170-180, it would have been a different game. Humbly admits that 140 was never going to be enough and also admits that they didn't bowl and field well. On their next game against Afghanistan, he says it is a do-or-die game for them. In the end, he thanks the supporters for coming in large numbers wherever they travel, and expects a similar kind of support in their last league game as well.

Sri Lanka's KAMIL MISHARA is adjudged the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his impressive match-winning performance. He scored an unbeaten 46 off 32 deliveries. Speaking about the instructions, he shares that Pathum had asked him to just play his natural game and take the innings deep. Reflecting on his performance, Mishara says it is a very happy feeling to win a game for his team. On his time away from the side, he adds that he always believed in himself and kept working hard for the opportunity.
... THE PRESENTATION ...

Earlier in the game, Sri Lanka invited Bangladesh to bat first. It was a slow burn, but all action-packed. Two back-to-back wicket maidens, one from Chameera and one from Thushara, set the tone for Sri Lanka. A self-inflicted run out, followed by a couple of dropped catches, and the bail not falling despite smashing the stump. It was all happening out there. Amidst it all, Hasaranga tied the batters in the middle overs with a miserly spell. However, a fighting unbeaten partnership between Jaker Ali and Shamim Hossain, of 86 runs, made the scorecard look quite more respectable and fighting than what could have been an ordinary one. Chameera was the pick from the seamers, while Hasaranga, on his return, did quite well with a couple of wickets.

How good has the top order been for the Lankans? Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis have been the pillars lately in white-ball cricket, doing the most heavy-lifting and easing the strain from the middle order. Add to it Kamil Mishara's emergence. Just 6 matches into his T20I career, he has appeared as a confident player at an important batting position, at number 3 on his comeback. Not to be very harsh, but an elevated challenge against the mighty Lankans proved too hot to handle for Bangladesh this time around. They do have a game left in this group stage, and it isn't going to be an easy one against Afghanistan by any means. Meaning, a win for them is a must in that clash. But before that, they have a lot to ponder and rethink about their strategies.

With the platform set and the required rate hovering just above a run a ball, it was about smart consolidation from there. That is the value of a strong start against a modest total. It forces errors from the bowlers, putting them on the back foot with too much to do. More than half of the runs were already chewed up even before halfway. And to be very fair, the bowling and fielding from Bangladesh were pretty ordinary. In fact, a shade of what they were against Hong Kong, China, in their opening game. There were a few consolation wickets towards the end, but Pathum Nissanka and Kamil Mishara's 95-run stand just took the wind out of the sails of Bangladesh.

Chasing 140 is rarely daunting in modern T20I cricket, but a solid start remains essential and a non-negotiable for any side. Though Kusal Mendis fell early, Pathum Nissanka anchored one end with composure. Kamil Mishara looked scratchy at first, but after being dropped early doors, he shifted gears and punished the bowlers. The Bangladeshi pacers could not match the effectiveness and conviction with which the Sri Lankan seamers operated. By the end of the Powerplay, Sri Lanka had taken control at 55/1.

Clinical. Dominating. Effortless. Perfect way to describe Sri Lanka's win against their arch-rivals. They are off to a flier in this tournament with a statement triumph, outnumbering the Bangladeshis across all departments. With 32 balls to spare and 6 wickets in hand, this will massively help Sri Lanka in terms of net run rate. On the other hand, a tough outing for Bangladesh as their net run rate takes a huge dent, and pushes them down to the third spot in Group B. Five matches into the Asia Cup, 2025, and all five have been one-sided in nature.

DONE AND DUSTED! Sri Lanka have defeated Bangladesh by six wickets with 32 balls to spare, giving their net run rate a significant boost. Short and outside off, Kamil Mishara punches it towards cover, where Rishad Hossain makes a fumble and lets the ball go through his hands towards sweeper cover. Both batters run the first one hard and push each other for the second after sensing an opportunity where the deep cover fielder gets a bit late, and even he has fumbled to his left, which allowed the batters to complete second run in time. It was a pretty one-sided affair.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Mishara has looked all but convincing so far! Fuller and outside off, Kamil Mishara looks to tonk it downtown, only to miss on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: An appeal for LBW from Sakib, but clearly missing the stumps. Extra bounce, on middle, on a length. Pathum Nissanka tries to whip that over square leg, but does not account for the ball popping off the deck. Misses and the ball thuds on the thigh pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Pathum Nissanka, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR LEG BYES! That could be really frustrating for Litton and his men! Short at 146 kph, on the bodyline, nipping into the batter. Pathum Nissanka misses to pull that away, and the ball deflects off the back thigh pad, and rolls between the keeper and the fielder at short third to race to the fence behind.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Pathum Nissanka, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Swings away at 141.1 kph, full and around off, Pathum Nissanka cracks the cover drive, but straight to the fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Lovely! Back of a length from Sakib, just outside off, nibbling away. Pathum Nissanka stands tall, reads the length early and punches it between the narrow gap at cover-point and backward point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Change. Just one over for Mustafizur Rahman despite taking a wicket. As the skipper, Litton Das has called in Tanzim Hasan Sakib into the attack.
Full and on middle, Pathum Nissanka forces the drive between mid off and cover for a single. Keeps the strike. Excellent over from Shoriful Islam. Just 4 off it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Shoriful Islam to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kamil is finally off the mark. Still streaky though. Good length, outside off. Kamil Mishara flashes hard on the up, and gets it off the outside edge. The ball flies over the backward point region for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Shoriful Islam to Kamil Mishara, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a good length, around off, Kamil Mishara mistimes the pull shot towards mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Shoriful Islam to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Swinging away, outside off, beyond the tramline. Mishara has a wild waft at it, away from the body. Misses and a wide is called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Shoriful Islam to Kamil Mishara, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Full and outside off, tapped away to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Shoriful Islam to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and shaping away, around off. Kamil Mishara prods forward and drives it to find the gap on the off side. But Rishad Hossain, at cover-point, stops it one-handed to his right. Kamil sniffs a single, but Rishad is quick to realise that and releases a flat throw toward the batter's end, but fails to score a direct hit. That will surely uplift the spirits in that Bangladeshi camp.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Shoriful Islam to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shapes into the batter, on middle, on a good length. Pathum Nissanka tries the pull shot, but miscues it off the inside edge. The ball rolls off the thigh pad towards the backward point region for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Shoriful Islam to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling into the left-hander, on a hard length. Kamil Mishara punches off the back foot to mid-wicket. A successful over for Mustafizur Rahman. 9 runs and a huge wicket of Kusal Mendis!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Mustafizur Rahman to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kamil Mishara is in at 3.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! A huge breakthrough early doors for Bangladesh and Mustafizur Rahman! He hurls it full in length, slanting across the batter. The ball lands and just nips away a shy bit, teasing the batter to have a poke at it. Kusal Mendis gets half forward and tries to drive it through the off side, but the ball nibbles away and takes the thick, healthy outside edge. Goes flat and low towards the right of the keeper. Litton Das flings himself towards the ball and gathers a fine catch behind the wickets before tumbling down onto the ground. Kusal Mendis departs for 3 (6) and Sri Lanka are 13/1, needing another 127 runs to win off 109 balls.
Commentary.Howout: c Litton Das b Mustafizur Rahman
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Mustafizur Rahman to Kusal Mendis, OUT! c Litton Das b Mustafizur Rahman.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a good length, outside off, angling away. Pathum cuts it off the back foot to deep point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Mustafizur Rahman to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! WOW! How good is that? Lands it short, does Mustafizur, on the leg stump line. Pathum Nissanka gets the ball at a comfortable height. Transfers the weight quickly onto the back foot and heaves it powerfully over deep mid-wicket for a cracking six. The first of the chase.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Mustafizur Rahman to Pathum Nissanka, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length, at 133.1 kph, on off. Kusal Mendis drives it on the rise, through cover-point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Mustafizur Rahman to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Reload! Angled across the batter, and miles outside off, beyond the tramline. Mendis leaves. Wide given.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Mustafizur Rahman to Kusal Mendis, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: 'The Fizz' starts on the money! Pitched outside leg, angling in on a length. Kusal Mendis gets behind the line and taps it to the right of the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Mustafizur Rahman to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mustafizur Rahman will bowl from the other end.
Short and outside off. Kusal Mendis leans back and ramps it on the bounce to deep third for a single. 4 off the first over for Sri Lanka. They need 136 runs off 114 deliveries.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Shoriful Islam to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Skids through, on off, on a length, at 135.5 kph. Kusal Mendis is a bit late to bring his bat down to block and chops it behind to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Shoriful Islam to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on middle, drilled down the ground, to the left of the bowler, and between mid on and mid off. A slight fumble by the mid off fielder allows them to cross over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Shoriful Islam to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Quick single! Full and around middle and off. Kusal Mendis gets right behind it and punches it in front of mid off and scampers for a single. Has to dive full length to get off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Shoriful Islam to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On the leg stump line, worked across to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Shoriful Islam to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Buzzers first up! Shoriful starts with a full ball, across off, Pathum Nissanka presses forward and taps it to the backward point region. Kusal Mendis is already halfway through for a single, but Pathum sees the fielder dive to his right and stop the ball. Denies for the single, and that forces Kusal to retreat back. Saif Hassan, the substitute fielder, throws it flat towards the bowler's end, but misses his shy, allowing Mendis to get home with the dive.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Shoriful Islam to Pathum Nissanka, No run.
